summary · 2,144 chars
TUI Travel PLC was a British leisure travel group headquartered in Crawley, West Sussex. The company operated in 180 countries.

The airlines that were child organizations or subsidiaries of TUI Travel PLC (or its predecessors/merged entities) include:
*   **Thomson Airways** (now TUI Airways): Described as the largest TUI-owned airline. It operates from 26 British airports. It was formed by the merger of Thomsonfly and First Choice Airways.
*   **First Choice Airways**: A charter airline based in Crawley, England. It flew to more than 60 destinations worldwide from 14 UK and Irish airports.
*   **Thomsonfly**: A British airline, previously known as Britannia.
*   **Britannia Airways**: The largest charter airline in the United Kingdom, rebranded as Thomsonfly in 2005. Its main bases were London Gatwick, London Luton, Birmingham, Manchester, Newcastle and Glasgow.
*   **Jet4you**: Operated services between Moroccan cities and destinations in France, Belgium, Switzerland, Spain and Italy.
*   **Corsair International**: Flies to 15 destinations in French overseas territories around the Mediterranean, Thailand, North Africa, and North America.
*   **Arkefly** (now TUI fly Netherlands): Operated charter flights from Amsterdam Schiphol.
*   **TUIfly** (now TUI fly Deutschland): A German leisure airline headquartered at Hannover Airport.
*   **Jetairfly** (now TUI fly Belgium): A Belgian airline with its administrative headquarters in Ostend.
*   **TUI fly Nordic**: Flies from Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Norway.
*   **Aladia Airlines**: A joint-venture with Mexican investors, launched in 2006. It was the only North American and Mexican airline part of the TUI Group.
*   **Britannia Nordic**: Flew from Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Norway.
*   **Hapag-Lloyd Express**: Based in Langenhagen, Germany.
*   **Hapag-Lloyd Flug**: Based in Langenhagen, Lower Saxony, Germany.
*   **Metrojet**: Based in Russia.
*   **Neos**: Based in Italy.

The countries linked to these airlines include the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Mexico, Morocco, Russia, and Italy.

summary · 845 chars
First Choice Airways Limited (originally Air 2000 Limited) was a British charter airline of European tour operator TUI Travel plc. It flew to more than 60 destinations worldwide from 14 UK and Irish airports. Its hubs were Birmingham Airport, London Gatwick Airport (primary hub), and Manchester Airport. The airline also operated scheduled year-round leisure routes to Cyprus and the resorts of Spain and Portugal. Long haul services to Mombasa in Kenya were introduced during the 1988/89 season. In 1993, scheduled operations commenced initially between London-Gatwick and Paphos, Cyprus. Over the next few years scheduled routes to Cyprus from Birmingham, Glasgow, Manchester and Newcastle were introduced. In 2000, additional scheduled services were introduced from eight UK airports to six major Spanish and Portuguese holiday destinations.

summary · 1,745 chars
TUI Travel PLC was a British leisure travel group headquartered in Crawley, West Sussex. The company operated in 180 countries.

The airlines associated with TUI Travel PLC include:
*   **Thomson Airways (now TUI Airways):** United Kingdom, Ireland. It is the largest TUI-owned airline and the largest charter airline in the world. It operates a fleet of 64 aircraft and flies from 26 British airports to 109 destinations worldwide. It was formed by the merger of Thomsonfly (formerly Britannia Airways) and First Choice Airways.
*   **First Choice Airways:** United Kingdom. It was a charter airline of European tour operator TUI Travel PLC, based in Crawley, England. It flew to more than 60 destinations worldwide from 14 UK and Irish airports.
*   **Thomsonfly:** United Kingdom. It was a British airline, previously known as Britannia and a business within TUI UK prior to September 2007.
*   **Britannia Airways:** United Kingdom. It was the largest charter airline in the United Kingdom, rebranded as Thomsonfly in 2005. Its main bases were London Gatwick, London Luton, Birmingham, Manchester, Newcastle and Glasgow.
*   **Corsair International:** France. It flies to 15 destinations in French overseas territories around the Mediterranean, Thailand, North Africa, and North America.
*   **Arkefly (now TUI fly Netherlands):** Netherlands.
*   **TUIfly (now TUI fly Deutschland):** Germany.
*   **Jetairfly (now TUI fly Belgium):** Belgium.
*   **TUI fly Nordic:** Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland.
*   **Aladia Airlines:** Mexico.
*   **Jet4you:** Morocco.
*   **Britannia Nordic:** Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland.
*   **Hapag-Lloyd Express:** Germany.
*   **Hapag-Lloyd Flug:** Germany.
*   **Metrojet:** Russia.
*   **Neos:** Italy.

summary · 918 chars
First Choice Airways Limited was a British charter airline of European tour operator TUI Travel plc. The airline was based in Crawley, England. It flew to more than 60 destinations worldwide from 14 UK and Irish airports. Its hubs were Birmingham Airport, London Gatwick Airport (primary hub), and Manchester Airport. It also operated scheduled year-round leisure routes to Cyprus and the resorts of Spain and Portugal. Long haul services included flights to the United States, Mombasa in Kenya, and other destinations. The airline started operations on 11 April 1987. In March 2008, the tourism division of the airline's parent group TUI AG, merged with First Choice Holidays PLC, forming the new company TUI Travel. Both Thomsonfly and First Choice Airways would be merged as Thomson Airways. On 23 April 2007, First Choice confirmed it is to close its bases at London Luton Airport and Cardiff from 1 November 2007.

summary · 1,236 chars
TUI Airways Limited (formerly Thomson Airways Limited) is the British arm of the TUI airline group, which is owned and operated by the TUI Group. The airline is the fourth largest UK airline by total passengers carried. Its head office and registered office is Wigmore House in Luton, Bedfordshire, United Kingdom.

TUI Airways has its origins in several rival airlines, including Euravia (founded in January 1962), Orion Airways (founded in 1979), and Air 2000 (founded in 1987). Britannia Airways was rebranded to Thomsonfly in May 2005 as its parent company Thomson Travel Group was bought by TUI Group. Thomsonfly and First Choice Airways merged following the merger of the travel divisions of TUI Group and First Choice Holidays in September 2007. The Thomson Airways brand was launched for the combined airline on 1 November 2008.

The investable enterprise and overall leadership formally merged with TUI to form London (LSE) and Frankfurt (DAX) listed TUI Group since December 2014. TUI Airways officially changed its legal name from Thomson Airways to TUI Airways on 2 October 2017.

The airline offers scheduled and charter flights from the United Kingdom and Ireland to destinations in Europe, Africa, Asia and North America.

summary · 730 chars
The television series *UK Uncovered* originates from the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom does not belong to the Schengen Area. The Schengen Area provides the travel benefit of abolished border controls at common borders, functioning as a system of open borders and a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes. Specifically, the Schengen Area allows for passport-free travel and freedom of movement between member states, where road, rail, and air passengers no longer have their identity checked by border guards when travelling between Schengen countries. The UK opted out of the Schengen Agreement to maintain its own border controls and to preserve the Common Travel Area with Ireland.

url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area
summary · 1,194 chars
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders that encompasses European countries that have officially abolished border controls at their common borders. It functions as a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes.

The United Kingdom does not belong to the Schengen Area. The UK declined to participate in the Schengen agreement and secured an opt-out from it. The UK chose not to join Schengen because it would not abolish border controls with any other countries. Additionally, the Republic of Ireland opted out of the Schengen Area to maintain the Common Travel Area (CTA) with the United Kingdom. The CTA, which has operated since 1923, provides passport-free travel and freedom of movement between the UK, Ireland, and the Crown Dependencies.

The travel benefit linked to the Schengen Area, which the UK is not part of, is the abolition of internal border controls and the implementation of a common visa policy. This allows for passport-free travel and free movement within the area for eligible nationals, and permits nationals of certain countries to enter via air, land, or sea without a visa for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period.

summary · 791 chars
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders that encompasses European countries that have officially abolished border controls at their common borders. It functions as a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes. The United Kingdom does not belong to the Schengen Area; it opted out of the Schengen Agreement to maintain the Common Travel Area with Ireland and the Crown Dependencies, which allows for passport-free travel and freedom of movement between these regions. Consequently, the travel benefit linked to the area the UK does not belong to is the ability to travel without border controls or visa requirements for short stays (up to 90 days within a 180-day period for certain nationals) across the internal borders of Schengen member states.

tool fetch #25 2026-06-22T08:50:50.535088+00:00
url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area
summary · 1,406 chars
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders that encompasses European countries that have officially abolished border controls at their common borders. It functions as a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes.

The United Kingdom does not belong to the Schengen Area. The UK declined to participate in the Schengen agreement and secured an opt-out from it. The UK chose not to join Schengen because it would not abolish border controls with any other countries. Additionally, the Republic of Ireland maintains an opt-out from the Schengen Area in order to maintain the Common Travel Area (CTA) between Ireland and the non-EU member United Kingdom. The UK, the Crown Dependencies, and the Republic of Ireland have operated the Common Travel Area since 1923, which allows for passport-free travel and freedom of movement among them.

The travel benefit linked to the Schengen Area is the abolition of internal border controls and a common visa policy. The common visa policy allows nationals of certain countries to enter the Schengen Area via air, land, or sea without a visa for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period. Within the Schengen Area, road, rail, and air passengers no longer have their identity checked by border guards when travelling between member states, and passport stamps are never issued when travelling between Schengen member states.

url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_effect
summary · 1,152 chars
"Border effect" refers to the tendency of people to purchase consumer goods in a locality that borders another jurisdiction where the desired good is either illegal or highly expensive. This phenomenon involves asymmetries in trade patterns between cities and regions of different countries and those located in the same country, with trade volume between different countries usually being much less. A 2017 meta-analysis of 1,271 estimates found that borders reduce trade by one third.

Examples of this effect include:
*   **Alcohol:** The small town of Whiteclay, Nebraska, which borders Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, was noted for selling alcohol to the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, where alcohol is illegal. This ended in 2017 when the town liquor stores' licenses were not renewed.
*   **Cannabis:** Since 2014, when legalized cannabis sales began in Colorado, the border effect has been observed in the United States. A notable example is Ontario, Oregon, which borders Idaho and opened cannabis dispensaries in 2019. Total cannabis sales from Ontario dispensaries topped $100 million in December 2020, fueled in part by Idaho customers.

url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area
summary · 1,674 chars
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders that encompass European countries that have officially abolished border controls at their common borders. It functions as a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes.

The United Kingdom is not part of the Schengen Area. The UK declined to participate in the Schengen agreement and secured an opt-out from it. The UK opted out in order to maintain the Common Travel Area (CTA) between Ireland and the United Kingdom, which has operated since 1923 with passport-free travel and freedom of movement. The Republic of Ireland also maintains an opt-out from the Schengen Area to preserve this Common Travel Area with the UK.

"Strange Little Girl" is a song by the American rock band The Black Keys. The country of origin is the United States. The United States is not part of the Schengen Area.

The Schengen Area provides the following types of travel and border arrangements:
*   **Abolition of internal border controls:** Road, rail, and air passengers no longer have their identity checked by border guards when travelling between Schengen countries.
*   **Common visa policy:** Nationals of certain countries can enter the Schengen Area via air, land, or sea without a visa for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period.
*   **Free movement:** About 1.7 million people commute to work across an internal European border each day. In 2015, there were 1.3 billion crossings of Schengen borders in total.
*   **External border checks:** Participating countries apply strict checks on travellers entering and exiting the Schengen Area, coordinated by the European Union's Frontex agency.

url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area
summary · 1,379 chars
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders that encompasses European countries that have officially abolished border controls at their common borders. It functions as a single jurisdiction under a common visa policy for international travel purposes.

The benefits provided to EU member states and the region include:

*   **Freedom of Movement:** The area allows for the free movement of people. About 1.7 million people commute to work across an internal European border each day, and in some regions, these international commuters constitute up to a third of the workforce.
*   **Economic Benefits:** Total trade between any two countries in the Schengen Area increases by approximately 0.1% per year. The removal of border controls is equivalent to the removal of a 0.7% tariff. The decrease in the cost of trade varies from 0.42% to 1.59% depending on geography, trade partners, and other factors. In 2015, there were 57 million crossings due to the transport of goods by road, with a value of €2.8 trillion.
*   **Travel Volume:** In 2015, there were 1.3 billion crossings of Schengen borders in total.
*   **Security Cooperation:** States in the Schengen Area have strengthened border controls with non-Schengen countries. The system includes the Schengen Information System (SIS), which allows for cooperation on crime, immigration, and other security-related matters.

summary · 951 chars
The FIFA World Cup trophy has been won by eight national teams. The specific winners and their title counts are:

*   **Brazil**: 5 titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002). Brazil is the only team to have played in every tournament.
*   **Germany**: 4 titles (1954, 1974, 1990, 2014). This count includes results representing West Germany (1954–1990).
*   **Italy**: 4 titles (1934, 1938, 1982, 2006).
*   **Argentina**: 3 titles (1978, 1986, 2022). Argentina are the reigning champions, having won their third title at the 2022 World Cup by defeating France.
*   **France**: 2 titles (1998, 2018).
*   **Uruguay**: 2 titles (1930, 1950). Uruguay was the inaugural winner in 1930.
*   **England**: 1 title (1966).
*   **Spain**: 1 title (2010).

Additionally, Uruguay displays four stars on their badge, representing their two World Cup titles and their two gold medals at the 1924 and 1928 Summer Olympics, which FIFA recognizes as World Championships.
